citation.ref: Besiroglu et al. 2024, Chinchilla Scaling: A replication attempt

provenance: Parametric loss L(N, D) = E + A/N^alpha + B/D^beta, the functional form of Hoffmann et al. 2022 ('Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models', NeurIPS 2022, Approach 3), with the constants re-estimated by Besiroglu et al. 2024 ('Chinchilla Scaling: A replication attempt', arXiv 2404.10102): E = 1.8172, A = 482.01, B = 2085.43, alpha = 0.3478, beta = 0.3658, copied verbatim from that paper (checked 2026-10-11). Hoffmann et al.'s own published estimates (E = 1.6934, A = 406.4, B = 410.7, alpha = 0.3392, beta = 0.2849) are kept in params for reference only: Besiroglu et al. show they come from optimiser early-stopping and rounding and imply ~70 tokens per parameter, inconsistent with Chinchilla's own 20; the re-estimated constants imply ~20. Training compute is approximated as C = 6ND FLOPs (Kaplan et al. 2020). The six points are DERIVED, not digitised: for each budget C = 1e20, 1e21, 1e22, 1e23, 1e24, 1e25 FLOPs, the minimum of L along N with D = C/(6N), found by a dense log-spaced search (6,000 steps over 1e7 to 1e13 parameters); y is that minimum loss. The page computes the same curves live from the params; src/lib/scalingLaw.test.ts pins the ~20 tokens-per-parameter optimum and the shrinking gain per tenfold budget.
